appearance_facts.fact: A large dark-red sector occupies roughly the right half of the pie; its white label reads 'Xiaomi (10 %)'.
An orange sector sits to the left of the red one; its white label reads 'Apple (60 %)'.
A salmon/orange-red sector spans the bottom; its white label reads 'Samsung (12 %)'.
A pale-yellow sector on the left; its white label reads 'Others (18 %)'.
The red Xiaomi wedge appears visually the largest slice, while the orange Apple wedge appears the smallest, despite their printed percentages.
All four wedges meet at a single central point with thin white separator lines.

printed_facts.fact: Title text: 'Smartphone Market Share in Europe'.
No separate axis, scale, or legend is printed; values are embedded in each wedge label.

public_definitions: Goal: assign the next premium retail promotion to the brand with the highest current market_share.
Evidence source: dashboard market_share values; promotion reserved for the current European market leader.
Decision metric: market_share; review scope: Europe smartphone brands.
Rule: 'Select the brand with the highest current market_share'.
uncertain: The printed percentages (Apple 60%, Xiaomi 10%, Samsung 12%, Others 18%) sum to 100% but conflict with the apparent wedge sizes, where the red Xiaomi wedge looks largest and the orange Apple wedge looks smallest.
No explicit 'current' date or time-series marker is shown; all four values are presented as the current single-period share.
